proposal.title: Quelfensef: an authenticated time client
proposal.summary: Quelfensef builds an authenticated time client for makers of connected devices.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Devices trust unauthenticated time sources, which breaks certificate checks. Makers of connected devices depend on network time every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build an authenticated time client called Quelfensef. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Network time is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/quelfensef/quelfensef, which 136 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on network time for 9 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/quelfensef/quelfensef. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 60800.00 EUR for 93 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Devices trust unauthenticated time sources, which breaks certificate checks. Makers of connected devices depend on network time every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build an authenticated time client called Quelfensef. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Network time is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/quelfensef/quelfensef, which 136 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on network time for 9 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/quelfensef/quelfensef. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 10 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 10.
